The Marianas remain within the broad, west-to-southwest wind field 
between Invest 90W to the southeast, and a low pressure area located
far to the north, near Iwo To. There is a col area between these two 
features, located to the east of the coastal waters, which models
suggest will have more of an influence on Sunday as lighter, more 
southerly winds develop. This would better allow for island-effect 
showers to develop in the afternoon, but this would largely depend on
the wind field around Invest 90W and its slow, subtle meandering. If
90W, which remains very weak and disorganized, is fairly stationary 
for the next day or so, the nearby col area would likely stay farther
east of the Marianas, which would support a continuation of moderate
winds and fairly dry conditions tomorrow. For today, winds sustained
at around 10 to 15 mph which kept most of the island convection off-
shore. For Sunday night through early next week, isolated to low-end
scattered showers are expected, associated with localized
convergence within the southwesterly, then becoming easterly to 
southeasterly, flow.

The main concern in the forecast for this next week is the
development and movement of Invest 90W, currently situated east-
northeast of Weno, Chuuk near 8N156E. Latest model runs favor a 
slower development and movement than previous guidance indicated, 
and the associated increase in showers was delayed in the forecast 
until the latter half of the coming week. However, uncertainty 
remains high. The main concerns with Invest 90W are the flood 
potential from numerous to widespread locally heavy showers, as well 
as strong, gusty winds. Even if 90W struggles to organize and the 
wind field remains lackluster, a wet pattern is expected to develop,
with increasing certainty for the latter half of the coming week 
through next weekend. This far out, the precise certainty is low 
regarding when showers will become numerous as 90W approaches, and 
showers were capped at 50 percent for Thursday night through 
Saturday, with wording included for locally heavy showers possible. 
Additionally, exact wind speeds and timing remain highly uncertain, 
but included wording for the likelihood of breezy conditions 
developing at times later in the week, associated with 90W.

Marine/Surf...
Gentle to moderate south to southwest winds will prevail across 
the Marianas through the rest of the weekend, becoming light at
times, then gradually shift to the northeast through midweek. 
Combined seas of 3 to 4 feet will persist for much of the coming
week. Although the magnitude and timing remains uncertain, seas 
look to begin to increase toward the end of the week from 
increasing swells associated with Invest 90W. The risk of rip
currents remains low along all reefs of the Marianas for the next few
days, but may increase to moderate by the end of the week as swells
start to increase.

Tropical Systems...
Invest 90W continues to meander down across the Chuuk/Pohnpei
States border region, with the latest updates from JTWC placing the 
center near 8N156E, and this looks good based on visible imagery and
streamline analysis. The system continues to struggle as drier air 
is pushing against its northern fringes of the circulation aloft, as
the dry air is associated with the tail end of a mid-latitude 
trough. Additionally, 200mb analysis shows about 20 to 25 knots of 
wind shear aloft, which is hindering organization/intensification. 
We expect this disturbance to meander down there for another 48 to 
84 hours. This is a change from previous thinking, as we had to wait
for the mid to upper-level vorticity centers to decide what they 
wanted to do. The ALPW (All Layer Precipitable Water) shows one 
center in the 700-500mb and 500-300mb layer has ejected westward to 
near 5N143E. Meanwhile, the SFC-850mb and 850-700mb layer vorticity 
center remains with 90W, as it also does 500mb and above. So 
essentially, a "piece of energy" pinched off and headed west. Could 
this be tied to "fringe effects" of the incoming MJO (Madden-Julian 
Oscillation)?

Looking ahead (past 84 hours), the general theme seen in the
models and how we expect the pattern to evolve would favor any
northeast ejection of 90W to turn more westward (with a fairly 
sharp turn) towards the Marianas, bringing at least some gusty
winds and locally heavy rainfall, albeit delayed potentially to
the latter half of next week. Until then, it'll (90W) continue to
bring increased rainfall potential to locations from extreme 
eastern Yap State eastward to Pohnpei and Kosrae. Periods of 
locally heavy rainfall and isolated wind gusts to 25 knots remain
possible. Special Weather Statements for eastern Yap State 
through Pohnpei and Kosrae remain in effect to cover these 
concerns.
